description: The 'Billing Rule Reader' role and the 'Billing Rule Readers' team (ebilling-r1 task 089d; owner 2026-11-03: 'yes Billing Administrator can have read on rules across whole organization'; shape by unified-access-control-r2, 2026-11-03). The 089b Exclude route (POST .../rule-overrides/exclude) checks the caller's own Read on the rule (sprk_policies), and Billing Administrator reads sprk_policy at Deep from the unit its holder is homed in, so a billing admin homed in a CHILD unit of the customer's top unit cannot read a rule owned in the top unit (403). This team fixes that in the role, not in the BFF. The team is created PER CUSTOMER business unit, in each customer's top business unit (the direct child of the root that provisioning H10 creates, the unit RestrictedContentOwnerTeam resolves), never in the root and never in Secure Record. Unlike the two owner teams in this script, it HAS members: the customer's child-unit billing admins. A team's Deep privilege is evaluated against the TEAM's business unit, so every member reads each rule owned in the customer's top unit and in every unit below it, and none owned in Secure Record, a sibling of the customer unit. Global Read, and Deep Read held in the root, are ruled out (D-123): both reach Secure Record. The role is created once in the root (Dataverse copies it into every child unit) and each customer unit's copy is assigned to that unit's team only. This file is the ONE list. scripts/Set-CustomerOwnerTeams.ps1 and RestrictedContentOwnerRoleGuardTests read it. Do not copy it anywhere else.
howToExtend: Do not add a table without evidence that the Exclude route (or another caller-checked route that needs org-wide rule Read) reads it AS THE CALLER. sprk_policyversion is not listed: on 2026-11-03 the Exclude route's only caller check on a rule is Read on sprk_policies (ProcedureAssignmentEndpoints.ExcludeTargets), and the one policy version it reads (the system-rule check) is read as the application (ProcedureAssignmentService.IsSystemRuleAsync, IGenericEntityService). RestrictedContentOwnerRoleGuardTests fails the build if this file lists any other table.

Never change 'depth'. Deep held by a team in the customer's top unit reaches that unit and its children only. Global reaches Secure Record, and so does Deep held in the root; Business Unit (Local) would not reach the child units. The guard and the script refuse any other depth for this file.

Members: each must hold 'memberPrivilege' (the billing-admin marker the BFF checks, BillingAdminAuthorization.WriteRuleSetPrivilege), so the team never gives an end user direct Read on rule configuration (D-185). Each must also be homed in the customer's top unit or a unit below it: a member from another customer's unit would read this customer's rules. The script never adds or removes a member: an operator adds each child-unit billing admin (customer deployment guide, Phase 7a) and -Verify fails while any member lacks the privilege or is homed elsewhere.

Then run, for each customer top business unit: scripts/Set-CustomerOwnerTeams.ps1 -EnvironmentUrl <url> -CustomerBusinessUnitId <id> (dry run), then -Apply (owner go), then -Verify. The same run sets up the two owner teams.

tables.reason: ebilling-r1 089b: the Exclude route's second filter checks the caller's Read on the rule (sprk_policies) before the billing-admin marker; uac-r2 kept that check (2026-11-03) and ruled out a filter that infers rule rights from Procedure rights. Deep from the customer's top unit gives each member Read on every rule owned there and below.
